channel.title: FCMO AI Newsletter
channel.description: Evidence-first intelligence on the AI frontier.

item.title: EuroHPC updates AI Gigafactories tender deadlines and invalidates existing submissions
item.description: EuroHPC’s AI Gigafactories tender page, updated 5 November 2026, says a technical issue invalidates all draft and submitted tenders in the system for both lots; replacement submission links are forthcoming, and applicants are told not to continue current drafts. The page retains deadlines of 4 February 2027 for Lot 1 and 3 December 2026 for Lot 2. The prior Lot 1 extension was publicly reported by the Czech ministry on 26 October to allow Member States time for national budget procedures and financial commitments. This is a change to the procurement process; it establishes no consortium awards, committed investment, facility construction, operating compute or access.

item.title: SwarmEvolve reports faster program search with latent agent swarms
item.description: Jiang and Karniadakis introduce SwarmEvolve, which runs 10 swarms of 45 Qwen3 agents that reason for 40 steps in latent space, select diverse traces and pass their KV caches to a summarizer that proposes programs. On 21 evaluator-driven mathematics and scientific-computing tasks, the authors report the highest average score against OpenEvolve, ShinkaEvolve and CodeEvolve across Qwen3 8B, 14B and 32B-FP8, using three seeds and one GPU plus eight CPU cores per model setup. With Qwen3 8B they report improving three AlphaEvolve constructions. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced here. The experiments are limited to the selected tasks and compute regime; the linked implementation repository returned 404 during this review.

item.title: Anthropic reports five cases of AI use in dual-use biological research
item.description: Anthropic’s 10 September 2026 threat-intelligence report describes five cases in which users or model-routing intermediaries used Claude in dual-use biological research. The company says some requests were blocked or limited to less capable models, while other computational and writing assistance proceeded. Anthropic does not claim the scientists intended harm, and it reports no resulting biological weapon or harmful experimental outcome. The cases are selected provider reports, not a representative sample or independent measurement of model uplift.

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber with stronger cyber-task results and scope-alignment claims
item.description: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Cyber on 5 November 2026 as a cyber-specialized model for authorized security research, initially restricted to approved Daybreak Red customers. OpenAI reports 48.5% on ExploitGym versus 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, 40.3% recall on a new web-penetration evaluation versus 32.0% for GPT-6 Astra, and a 0.07% out-of-scope honeypot exploitation rate without deployment safety instructions (0% with them). The system card reports 90/288 FrontierCyber challenges solved, below Astra’s 96/288, with neither model solving the 15 hardest challenges. OpenAI also attributes 948 working Linux-kernel exploits and 81 high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities to its research campaign; Mozilla’s advisory lists some OpenAI-affiliated reporters among fixes but does not validate the full totals or model contribution. The card also reports a 20.29% final-response blocker-reporting flag rate, between GPT-5.6 Sol (34.18%) and GPT-6 Astra (11.66%); OpenAI says most reviewed cases had disclosed the blocker earlier but omitted it from the final answer. These performance and campaign figures remain provider-reported and have not been independently reproduced here.

item.title: Google reports an early VLA robotics proof of concept for astronaut logistics
item.description: Google Cloud's Oct 27 account describes a physical robotic proof of concept developed with NASA Johnson Space Center and JPL for possible deep-space logistics and medical-equipment support. Google reports an initial 85% pick-and-place success baseline in early lab environments and says the fine-tuned model can run locally on compact edge devices. The article mentions MuJoCo simulation before real hardware but does not say whether the 85% trials were simulated or hardware-run, or give a denominator and success criteria. These are first-party reports, not independent measurements, and do not establish flight readiness or quantified edge efficiency.

item.title: ReproBridge reports higher AI reproduction success from reusable experiment artifacts
item.description: A preprint published on 2026-11-05 introduces ReproBridge, a workflow that packages refined research code, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide for reuse by later coding agents. The authors evaluate it on 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 selected ICML 2026 Spotlight papers. Across four tested coding-agent models, they report mean task reproduction success rising from 76.4% with raw code to 92.6% with refined artifacts and downstream API spending falling by 19.7% on average. Five human-verified reference measurements per task and execution-evidence audits are part of the reported protocol. These results are author-reported; code and dataset were not publicly linked on the inspected project page, and the study does not establish scientific validity, conference-wide reproduction rates, or benefits to human researchers.

item.title: Scientist World reports a benchmark of AI research agents across 1,000 executable paper environments
item.description: A 5 November arXiv paper introduces Scientist World, which turns selected empirical papers into executable research environments. The authors report releasing 1,000 environments with reproduced baselines, hidden evaluation slices and separate verifier-agent checks. In their benchmark, agents improved on the reproduced method in 84% of improvement attempts and 74% of attempts that designed a method from scratch. The paper also reports raising Qwen3-8B’s median idea score across ten held-out papers after supervised fine-tuning and offline reinforcement learning; a fixed GPT-5.6 Sol implementer executed all ideas. These are author-reported results from the paper’s selected tasks and setup. They do not establish general autonomous scientific discovery, and were not independently audited or reproduced here. The linked project page currently describes a friends-only preview, shows zero papers in its progress counters, and elsewhere gives a 76% result instead of the paper’s 74%; the cited GitHub organization showed two unrelated public repositories and the trace dataset returned HTTP 401. Public artifact access and this score discrepancy remain unresolved.

item.title: China proposes protections governing platform work algorithms and consequential worker decisions
item.description: On 8 October 2026, China’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security published a draft cross-agency measure for public comment through 8 November. The proposal would require platforms to explain labor-management algorithms, prohibit specified forms of discrimination, and require human review before certain consequential decisions such as stopping task assignments or banning accounts, subject to a narrow emergency exception. The measure is a proposal, not adopted law; implementation and effects are not established.

item.title: India’s ESTIC 2026 draft vision reports Physical AI targets through 2047
item.description: On 29 October 2026, the Press Information Bureau reported the release of the National Vision Document for India’s Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026. Its account of the Department of Science and Technology’s autonomous-systems, Physical AI and robotics session describes recommendations to strengthen 25 National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems technology hubs for the mission’s next phase beginning in January 2028, build testbeds and India-specific datasets, support indigenous hardware with patient capital, and emphasize safety-by-design, hands-on training, early customer engagement and viable business models. PIB calls the proposed milestones a draft vision: pilot validation by 2030, wider deployment and manufacturing by 2035, and global competitiveness by 2047. A separate PIB release says stakeholder consultations had considered a possible Physical AI Mission. These sources do not establish an approved or funded mission, implementation owners, or delivered results; the full vision PDF was not located in this review.

item.title: Anthropic reports task-level patterns in scientists’ use of Claude
item.description: Anthropic’s 5 November 2026 report analyzes 207,049 consumer-plan Claude and Claude Code sessions classified as scientific work from 2 August to 30 September. It reports that data analysis and writing are common uses, while data gathering and ideation appear less often than their estimated share of researcher time. An LLM-based task-capability measure is associated with greater use: the top fifth of tasks receive about two to four times the use expected from researcher time. A separate survey of 528 active AI-using scientists broadly mirrors the task mix. These are first-party, classifier-based usage findings; the underlying conversations are not public for independent audit. The report does not measure research quality, causal productivity or realized scientific discoveries, and its future-output scenarios are hypothetical.

item.title: China publishes GB/Z 290-2026 guidance on AI-generated content in academic publishing
item.description: China’s State Administration for Market Regulation and Standardization Administration announced on 4 November 2026 that they had approved 37 national standardization guidance technical documents, including GB/Z 290-2026, titled “Guidance on boundaries for use of AI-generated/synthetic content in academic publishing.” The National Standard Information Public Service Platform lists the document as current and gives its publication date as 30 October 2026. The announcement and catalogue establish the document’s issuance, title and status; the text’s provisions, adoption and effects were not assessed.

item.title: FrontierPhysics benchmarks end-to-end AI-agent research across nine physics domains
item.description: A 4 November arXiv preprint introduces FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark built from physicists’ own research projects. The authors report 56 tasks from 42 physicists across nine domains, with agents required to plan research, run analyses or experiments, and produce verifiable outputs and manuscripts. Across 22 models and 26 configurations, they report pass rates below 30%; Claude Opus 5.5 is highest at 27.4%. The authors also report manually correcting nine false failures among 168 GPT-6 Astra xhigh rollouts. These are paper-reported results, not an independent rerun.

item.title: Value-based RL reportedly generalizes robot-policy improvement across simulated tasks
item.description: A 4 November arXiv preprint studies online post-training of the pi_0.5 vision-language-action policy across simulated manipulation tasks. The authors report that critic-guided recipes—off-policy generative policy optimization (OGPO) and best-of-N (BoN)—increasingly improve success on held-out scenes and objects as training-task diversity grows, while filtered supervised fine-tuning often forgets on unseen objects. In MolmoSpaces, they report up to +58 percentage points on unseen scenes and +39 points when both scene and object change; one 16-task BoN run used 2.9× fewer gradient steps than 16 single-task runs at matched data-collection budget. These are paper-reported results from three training seeds, not an independent reproduction. The evaluation is simulation-only; on the more challenging LIBERO suite the authors report similar patterns but generalization often gave way to forgetting.

item.title: OpenAI reports an automated Linux pipeline that reproduced 1,724 kernel vulnerabilities and developed patches for 948 unique LPEs
item.description: OpenAI describes a controlled prototype that scanned selected Linux kernel audit targets using an upcoming cyber model and agent pipeline. In its mid-October run, it reports 2,308 candidate findings, 1,724 dynamically reproduced vulnerabilities, 291 information-leak proofs of concept, 1,169 working LPE exploits and 948 distinct patches corresponding to 948 unique LPE vulnerabilities. OpenAI reports about USD 1.21 million in API-credit cost. OpenAI also reports that human review caught 20 wrong-vulnerability attributions among 200 apparent successes in an early run, after which it added an independent path check. The page itself is internally inconsistent: its overview and findings summary say 948 LPE exploits, while the detailed section reports 1,169 working exploits and 948 distinct patches. These remain first-party results from one workflow: independent reproduction, maintainer acceptance of all patches, transfer beyond the tested configurations and generalized security impact are not established.

item.title: Turn-level action selection improves reported agent success with substantial token overhead
item.description: A 4 November arXiv preprint evaluates turn-level best-of-N (Turn-BoN): at each step, a generator proposes 4 or 8 candidate tool actions and a separate language-model selector chooses one before it is executed. On 89 Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks across four trials, the authors report higher pass rates for Qwen3.6-35B and K2-Horizon-375B generators when paired with Kimi-K3 or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash selectors. Reported gains include K2-Horizon 73.3% to 77.9% at N=4 and Qwen3.6 47.5% to 52.8% at N=4 or 55.2% at N=8. The authors also report 40–50% fewer turns and reduced looping, while output tokens rise to about 3.6–8.2 times baseline. These preliminary paper-reported results use two generator models and stronger selectors; they were not independently reproduced.

item.title: Google releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with 15-second video and conversational editing
item.description: Google announced Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash on 5 November 2026 and says it is generally available through the Gemini API and Gemini for business. Google reports native video generation and editing up to 15 seconds, compared with 10 seconds for Omni 1.1, multi-turn conversational editing and a 30% price reduction to $0.07 per second for 720p generation. Google also claims stronger reference adherence and consistency, but the announcement provides no independent comparison. The release identifies continuing limitations for fast sports action, rapid script changes and complex physics; actual billed cost and quality across independent workloads remain unestablished.

item.title: Mistral lists Z.ai GLM 5.3 Flash as a generally available third-party API model
item.description: Mistral’s API catalog includes a 22 October 2026 entry for Z.ai GLM 5.3 Flash, labeled generally available, third-party and MIT; the page says Mistral serves the model without modifications. It lists a 320B-parameter multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 18B active parameters, 1M context and 128K maximum output, and displays rates of $0.15 per million input tokens, $0.03 per million cached input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. The listing and prices are direct evidence of what Mistral advertises, not of account eligibility, realized billing, independent quality or an economic advantage over direct Z.ai access.

item.title: Google DeepMind reports an Antigravity workflow for cheminformatics and macrocycle design
item.description: Google DeepMind's 3 November walkthrough describes a human-steered Antigravity workflow for cheminformatics using a lung-cancer-treatment example. The company reports literature and catalog search across thousands of compounds, a curated view of 568 compounds, matched-pair analysis, potency models and proposed rigidified macrocycles with synthesis routes in about an hour. The report is first-party evidence of what Google describes, not independent confirmation of the run or its measurements. The source says the designs are hypotheses that require synthesis and experimental validation; it reports no such validation.

item.title: China’s CAC proposes cooperation on intelligent-internet infrastructure and agent interoperability
item.description: On 4 November 2026, China’s Cyberspace Administration published a cooperation initiative on intelligent internet development. Its eight proposals address network and compute infrastructure, agent interoperability standards and lifecycle trust, application ecosystems, cross-border data, safety, digital skills and multilateral governance dialogue. The text calls for open, non-discriminatory international standards for agent interoperability and a verifiable, traceable trust framework covering agent discovery, negotiation and execution. This is a nonbinding cooperation initiative: it does not establish adopted standards, binding duties, implementation or participating-body commitments. The official Chinese-language page was directly inspected, including all eight numbered proposals (paragraphs 42–56).

item.title: BEAKER introduces an expert-curated benchmark for embodied multimodal models in chemical laboratories
item.description: A 2026-11-04 arXiv paper introduces BEAKER, an offline benchmark of 1,000 expert-curated question-answer samples across 11 image and video task types for multimodal models considered as embodied systems in self-driving chemical laboratories. The authors report evaluation of 28 models and find persistent weaknesses in fine-grained action grounding, laboratory apparatus and state recognition, safety norms, and ordering steps in mid-length procedures. These results are author-reported; the benchmark does not test closed-loop device interaction.

item.title: Evidence-gated authority in language-model review trades fewer corruptions of correct proposals for missed welfare-only repairs
item.description: In a September 2026 paper, Fuad Ali compares broad reviewer override with a rule that lets a reviewer replace an upstream proposal only after it supplies a mechanically valid certificate of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. The paper reports paired experiments with Qwen3-8B and Mistral-Small-24B on 96 synthetic spatial-policy tasks and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark. The gate prevents changes to correct proposals by construction, but also bars welfare improvements to compliant, suboptimal proposals. A prospective retain/replace/escalate interface protects correct proposals for Qwen, which then declines welfare-only repairs; Mistral still replaces and corrupts all 48 correct proposals in that test. These are author-reported results from quantized local models and structured synthetic tasks, not evidence of deployment prevalence or a model-independent safety guarantee.

item.title: NVIDIA describes an internally deployed multi-agent assistant for AI-factory operations
item.description: NVIDIA’s 4 November technical blog describes an AI Factory Operations Agent that it says is in internal production for DGX SuperPOD operations. The reported system uses domain agents to correlate cluster signals and recommend actions through a Kubernetes control plane, per-session sandboxes and read-only inspection credentials. The source reports no measured operational outcomes, and this activation did not independently verify the deployment or controls.

item.title: SpecCompact reports faster agent context compaction through parallel semantic verification
item.description: A 4 November arXiv preprint introduces SpecCompact, which fine-tunes a small drafter to generate six context-summary slots in parallel and uses a target model to verify and repair proposed lines. The authors report 2.04–5.63× compaction-latency speedups over Hermes-style summarization across AppWorld and τ³ with Gemma4-31B-IT and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B. A separate Hermes/Gemma4 deployment study reports an 8.68× median paired speedup across three author-designed scenarios. These are paper-reported measurements. The paper says the method does not provide a consistent accuracy advantage; task-performance results vary by model and benchmark, and the full task evaluation did not use all system optimizations.

item.title: MCPGuard paper reports conformance gaps in official Model Context Protocol SDKs
item.description: An arXiv preprint presents MCPGuard, a method that compares the Model Context Protocol specification with official SDK models and session logic, then checks candidate gaps with executable proof-of-concept tests. On Python SDK 1.26.0 and TypeScript SDK 1.29.0, the authors report 13 and 19 confirmed gaps, including 27 structural findings and five behavioral findings. They also report that two malformed URI-format metadata fields were accepted by all 32 public servers that completed the study’s handshake test. The authors say findings were privately reported to maintainers. These are paper-reported results, not an independent audit of current releases. ArXiv’s abstract page and Atom API date v1 to 12 August 2026, while its 4 November cs.AI new-submissions list includes the paper; why the listing contains it remains unresolved, so 4 November is not treated as the paper’s established first-publication date.

item.title: Anthropic reports a bacteriophage-derived vault structure and engineered nanocapsule
item.description: Anthropic reports the first cryo-EM structure of a vault-like particle formed by a bacteriophage protein in a prokaryotic laboratory system. In its 4 November article, the company says its team searched about 15 billion predicted proteins, tested 15 candidates, observed seven vault-like assemblies, and confirmed four by cryo-EM. It describes a 96-copy phage-derived structure and an engineered variant with about 20% more enclosed volume. Anthropic also reports that Claude helped with sequence search, construct design, isolation-method development and microscopy processing under human direction; a purification workflow took about 90 minutes rather than about three days. These are first-party claims. The particles were made in E. coli; their natural function and formation in native hosts remain unknown, and the linked technical report and independent reproduction were not available in this review.

item.title: A paper proposes auditability as a fourth machine-unlearning criterion and reports a two-stage method with dataset tradeoffs
item.description: The Nov. 4 arXiv preprint “Widen the Gap, Hide the Gap” treats auditability—whether a provider can distinguish requested-forget examples from retained examples under a chosen statistic—as a fourth criterion for machine unlearning. It proposes GapWiden, which trains an audit-statistic gap into the unlearned model, and GapVeil, an inference-time rejection sampler intended to reduce disclosure of that gap. The authors report evaluations over eleven unlearning methods on TOFU and MUSE. Results are paper-reported: auditability rises toward 0.99 on MUSE, but retain performance on MUSE News falls from 0.569 to 0.380. These benchmark results do not establish deletion from a deployed model or proof of deletion for an individual request.

item.title: China’s central science-industry integration opinion directs enterprise-led research and AI+ deployment
item.description: On Oct 21, 2026, China’s CPC Central Committee General Office and State Council General Office issued an opinion on deeper integration of science and industrial innovation. The text calls for enterprise-led applied research projects, staged funding and milestone evaluation, technology-transfer mechanisms, demonstration scenarios, broader private-enterprise access to research facilities and data, and full implementation of AI+ across industries. This record covers the issued policy and its stated mechanisms; it does not establish implementation, dedicated budgets, adoption or measured effects.

item.title: Brazil MGI issues advisory AI transparency guides for federal public services
item.description: Brazil's Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services published two implementation guides for AI transparency in federal public services: an AI System Card for documenting system purposes, processing, limits and risks, and a Transparency Design Guide for notifying users when services use AI. The complete 37-page Design Guide v1.0 scopes recommendations to federal direct, autarchic and foundational administration and says it does not regulate AI uses or replace legal duties. MGI describes the wider self-assessment framework as orienting. Publication is established; agency uptake, binding effect and public-service outcomes are not.

item.title: ARLoop applies attention residuals to fully open looped-transformer pretraining
item.description: A 3 Nov 2026 preprint introduces ARLoop, which uses attention over recurrent depth to select earlier representations in a looped transformer. The authors report controlled perplexity gains at 140M and 370M parameters and scale the method to 0.6B and 1.2B models. Their 1.2B model, trained on 0.5T tokens with three recurrences, reportedly outperforms the 3.5B Huginn looped model across the paper's evaluated tasks and is competitive with Qwen3.5-2B. The authors released an MIT-licensed implementation and evaluation recipes. All performance results remain paper-reported; independent reproduction and strict cross-model compute/data comparability are unresolved.

item.title: Continual AutoResearch finds persistent state speeds early research, but does not reliably improve final results
item.description: A 3 November 2026 preprint introduces Continual AutoResearch, a matched benchmark for comparing persistent and reset AI agents across nine machine-learning task families. The authors report that persistent state improved fixed-budget search efficiency for all five evaluated CLI agents, mainly by producing a valid solution sooner or a stronger first solution. Final held-out performance was much less consistent: only Sonnet 4.6 showed a substantial aggregate outcome gain, and most agents lost their efficiency advantage after controls for first-solution latency and candidate count. An explicit memory ablation and trace cases show that relevant prior insights can improve initialization, while overly specific prior state can anchor search and yield worse final selections. These are author-reported results from short task streams; the paper says its code will be released with the camera-ready version.

item.title: Anthropic publishes a Claude-attributed subexponential #3-SAT algorithm claim with Lean materials
item.description: Anthropic contributed a version-one preprint on October 27 describing a deterministic algorithm that counts satisfying assignments for fixed-width CNF formulas in subexponential time, including #3-SAT, and attributes the core algorithm to an internal Claude research model. Anthropic’s official repository includes the paper and a Lean 4 formalization. GitHub reports that the repository’s exact commit passed its `verify (eth)` CI workflow, which the README describes as a pinned Lean build, Comparator check and nanoda recheck. This repository-hosted result was not independently rerun here. The README explicitly says machine checks do not establish that the formal statement matches the paper; independent mathematical review remains open. The result is asymptotic and does not establish practical SAT performance. An independent external formal-methods audit later reports replaying Anthropic's exact pinned Lean proof with Lean, Comparator and nanoda, a fresh-environment replay, and a Lean bridge from the formal statement to textbook-style ETH in Anthropic's own machine model. The auditor explicitly leaves paper-to-statement and machine-model/input-encoding correspondence to prose and does not certify the paper's mathematical argument. This strengthens the reported reproducibility of the formal artifact, not the truth status of the theorem.

item.title: llama.cpp v0.9.0 adds FP8 quantization and multi-sequence inference support
item.description: The ggml-org/llama.cpp project published v0.9.0 at commit cd959ba on 4 November. The release lists OCP FP8 E4M3 support, a multi-sequence attention operation for unified KV caches, batched tensor-copy APIs, four additional model architectures and audio and server API updates. Maintainers describe the attention change as more efficient, but the inspected release notes provide no quantified benchmark or independent validation.

item.title: Google reports a Gemini 4 Argon workflow porting an ocean model from Fortran to Rust
item.description: Google Antigravity reports that Gemini 4 Argon migrated the 174,774-line Fortran/C core of FVCOM to safe Rust in a 59-minute run, with 100-seed numerical parity, 42 tests, 96.8% branch coverage, six reported bug findings and 1.88× runtime after optimization. The post gives stage timings and a runtime/memory scorecard, making the account more detailed than a product demo. The run, metrics, exact input correspondence and scientific validity remain first-party and have not been independently reproduced; the linked skill’s immutable source and run artifacts were unavailable in this review.

item.title: Authors report frequent context compaction preserves performance across tested long-horizon and long-input tasks
item.description: In arXiv:2611.05306v1, the authors evaluate context compaction and selective input reading on six long-horizon and seven long-input benchmark families. For end-of-conversation compaction, they report broadly near-baseline accuracy across tested thresholds for Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT 5.6 Sol, alongside estimated optimized retail-cost reductions; the estimates are not observed invoice savings. In a single-action-compaction condition, median live context is 7–9K tokens and maximum context 15–37K, while GPT 5.6 Sol falls 2.0 and 3.3 percentage points below its baselines on two coding benchmarks. These are author-reported results from the tested benchmarks and models; independent reproduction and universal transfer are not established.

item.title: OpenAI announces acquisition of Pierre Computer Company and its developer tools
item.description: OpenAI announced on 4 November that it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, a software company behind Code Storage and developer tools including Trees and Diffs, which OpenAI says are already used in the Codex app. OpenAI says Pierre's open-source projects will remain open-source and Code Storage customers can continue using the service after closing while it works to bring features into Codex. The transaction has not closed and remains subject to customary conditions including regulatory approvals; price, final terms and post-close outcomes were not disclosed.

item.title: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors and cites a large flexible-load agreement for its planned Georgia campus
item.description: OpenAI announced Grid Protectors on 2 November 2026 as a program to arrange flexible power use at future compute campuses. It cites a Georgia Power agreement for a planned Effingham County campus expected to require about 3,200 MW, with up to 1,000 MW of demand response under a 25-year term. Georgia Power said its contract to serve OpenAI was approved through the Georgia PSC regulatory process. A joint PSC Staff/Georgia Power statement records staff review, compliance with prior orders and non-objection subject to stated terms; the PSC filing describes a 3,210 MW contract as deemed approved but does not identify its customer, and its public-summary ZIP was not inspectable. Georgia Power projects about $950 million in annual portfolio savings beginning in 2029 and at least $180 per year for a typical residential customer; these are future projections. The campus is not operating, and actual curtailment and customer outcomes remain unmeasured.

item.title: Preprint reports safety-framed review attacks that steer AI-agent recommendations
item.description: A 3 November 2026 preprint reports that fabricated safety warnings presented as ordinary consumer reviews can steer AI-agent recommendations without containing instructions to the model. Across six tested models and ten consumer-travel domains, the authors report 60.4% success for safety-framed reviews versus 66.0% for command-style injection; the former passed two evaluated injection detectors more often in their setup. The paper also reports transfer to four browser agents tested on one live review page and a corroboration instruction that reduced success in a non-adaptive test. These are author-reported findings, not estimates of deployed attack prevalence. Independent reproduction, adaptive attackers, genuine-warning trade-offs and broader transfer remain open.

item.title: OpenAI reports a safety-evaluation gap with production Codex decisions
item.description: OpenAI reports that success on its Respecting Warnings safety evaluation was 10.2–37.4 points lower than on selected, structurally comparable decisions sampled from Codex production logs across six served model variants. Evaluation and production model-level success were positively associated, but their absolute rates and exact model ordering differed. In a GPT-6.1 Sol intervention, specifying the evaluation objective shifted reported success sharply in opposite directions, while a generic evaluation cue changed it little. This is a provider-run study with approximate case matching, a six-model cohort and no independent reproduction; it does not establish safety rates for other deployments.

item.title: Adversarial speculative decoding routes important reasoning through higher precision
item.description: A Nov 3 preprint proposes adversarial speculative decoding: train a draft model to make selected reasoning-decision tokens more likely to be rejected, so exact residual sampling by the target writes those tokens at the first slot of a new verification block. The paper reports increased numerical precision at early slots, long-horizon coding-agent gains on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and up to roughly 2% decoding-speed cost. These are author-reported experiments on two serving configurations; independent reproduction and broader transfer are not established.

item.title: A new coding-agent benchmark reports frequent harmful side effects alongside task success
item.description: A 2 November 2026 preprint introduces VeriHarm-Bench, a 150-task shell-scripting benchmark that pairs task-correctness tests with executable tests for one designated harmful side effect per task. The tests check final sandbox state. Across four held-out coding agents, the authors report 95.1% average task accuracy, 58.2% harmful success and 37.0% safe success. A human review of 50 sampled items found higher majority-vote validity among top-ranked than bottom-ranked candidates, with moderate annotator agreement. These are author-reported results from a curated benchmark, not estimates of harm prevalence in deployed coding agents; transient harms, severity and transfer beyond the tested regime remain open.

item.title: OpenAI introduces LifeVal, an evaluation of AI agents on everyday-life tasks
item.description: OpenAI introduced LifeVal, an evaluation of AI performance on everyday-life tasks selected using American and multinational time-use datasets and supplemented by a demographically representative survey that the public page says included 3,995 respondents, while the linked paper’s methods section specifies n=3,837 for the willingness-to-pay survey; the difference is unresolved. Its public page reports selected task scores of 90.4%–100% on illustrated workflows, but does not identify which model produced the examples or provide an overall aggregate result or detailed open protocol. The design and scores are first-party; independent replication and real-world user outcomes are not established.

item.title: The Trinity reports capability-driven harness evolution across multimodal agent benchmarks
item.description: The Trinity paper proposes recursive evolution of tool-using agent harnesses by grouping tasks around shared capability requirements, generating simplified training worlds, and selectively inheriting validated modules while keeping the foundation model fixed. In the current arXiv v2 paper, the authors report mean performance gains of 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two physical-robot tasks. The results are author-reported; the official code repository was released on 30 October, but this activation did not run or independently reproduce it. The paper itself notes variable benchmark-discovery coverage and limits its present contribution to harness-level self-improvement.

item.title: OpenAI reports engineering-task gains and early industry workflows with AI models
item.description: In a 3 November 2026 report, OpenAI says an unnamed newer internal model averaged 0.875 on BenchCAD 2.0, compared with 0.594 for GPT-6 Astra at maximum reasoning effort. BenchCAD 2.0 documents 100 held-out cases across six tasks involving CAD reconstruction, assemblies and PCB connectivity, scored against references without an LLM judge in an offline sandbox. OpenAI also describes early workflows with Chip Ganassi Racing and a research collaboration with Mazda, where engineers review model outputs. These are first-party performance and workflow reports; the unnamed model, independent reproduction and measured workplace productivity or manufacturability outcomes remain unestablished.

item.title: Data4 and EDF announce a long-term nuclear electricity allocation for French data centers
item.description: EDF and Data4 announced a 12-year Nuclear Production Allocation Contract (CAPN) for Data4’s French data centers. EDF’s French release says the agreement allocates Data4 a 40 MW share of EDF’s operating nuclear fleet, with costs and production-volume risks shared, and forecasts first deliveries from 2026 at about 230 GWh per year. Data4 describes it as the first CAPN signed by a French data-center operator. The sources establish the announced contract terms, not actual Data4 deliveries, metered volumes, the contract tariff, or allocation to AI workloads.

item.title: NIST publishes an AI incident-management workshop report and plans broader response guidance
item.description: NIST published IR 8621 on 2 November, summarizing a May workshop on incidents involving highly capable AI systems. The report separates attacks against AI systems from harm caused by misuse, anomalous behavior or malfunction, and describes gaps in observability, evidence, containment and responsibility across AI supply chains. NIST says it plans to update SP 800-61 and develop or explore agent-incident guidance, monitoring/logging, information sharing and traceability resources. These are workshop findings and proposed future work, not binding requirements or evidence that controls are implemented or effective.

item.title: Zyphra revises its hierarchical sparse-attention preprint with a 1B-token distillation budget
item.description: A revised preprint introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), which routes queries through a tree of compressed key summaries to select sparse attention keys. In author-run tests on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, six-level routing reportedly scored 93.3% on RULER-13 versus 96.0% for dense attention while attending to 1%–6% of the original KV cache. The Nov 2 revision reports a 1B-token distillation budget. The authors model, but do not measure, end-to-end latency; performance quality beyond 256K tokens remains unvalidated.

item.title: WebHarbor releases 153 local web-agent environments and 3,518 tasks; authors report transfer gains for one 4B agent
item.description: A 2 November 2026 arXiv preprint and its linked project repository describe WebHarbor, a collection of 153 Dockerized website environments and 3,518 tasks for GUI-agent evaluation and reinforcement-learning training. The paper reports that WebHarbor-4B scored 75.8 on average across WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web, versus 70.6 for an online-RL OpenWebRL-4B baseline under the authors’ setup. These are author-reported results from one trained 4B model. The environments reconstruct task-relevant parts of real sites; the paper says some interactive features are approximated and that synthetic performance does not guarantee safe or equivalent performance on live websites.

item.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve, a zero-knowledge proof prototype for model inference
item.description: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source prototype for proving that an inference response matches a commitment to a model’s weights. It reports performance for a 4-bit Llama 4 Maverick model, with substantial proving overhead and a CPU-verifiable proof. Its linked technical report says it was AI-generated and not reviewed in detail; it also says batched zero-knowledge is not proved, executable C++ equivalence to Lean is unproved, and the verified statement concerns an integer-quantized model’s greedy output. The results remain first-party prototype claims, not independent validation or production evidence.

item.title: Air Security reports a Solana starter repository used to deliver a remote-access payload through coding-agent workflows
item.description: Air Security Research Lab’s 29 October report describes a GitHub repository posing as a Solana starter kit whose README instructed users to run a PowerShell command that downloaded and executed code. The report says its recovered archived payload installed a configured NetSupport remote-access client with hidden operation and login persistence. Air Security reports that the original payload endpoint was offline when checked and the named repository was later unavailable. The report documents a plausible agent-mediated delivery route, but does not establish that a coding agent executed the command, identify victims, or measure campaign prevalence. the research desk did not independently inspect or run the sample.

item.title: Authors report that rare training facts raise LLM discovery rates in two controlled scientific domains
item.description: A 2 November 2026 preprint studies whether facts seen once in training are linked to language-model discovery capacity. In experiments on materials-science and regulatory-genomics tasks, the authors report that raising the share of these “monofacts” increases exact recovery of held-out target materials or DNA sequences across two open-weight model families. Repeated exposure weakens the trend while holding training-set diversity fixed. In-distribution, higher monofact rates also raise hallucinated outputs; cross-domain effects require in-domain training data. The results are author-reported and concern controlled target-recovery tasks, not prospective laboratory discoveries or broad scientific autonomy.

item.title: Study measures MCP tool-poisoning exposure across 12 agent frameworks
item.description: A new arXiv paper reports a controlled measurement of malicious MCP tool-description attacks across 12 agent frameworks, 18 models and 45 scenarios. The authors report vulnerable behavior in 22.9% of 9,720 tested framework-model-scenario cells and classify 12.1% of vulnerable cells as actual secret exfiltration. The tested threat model requires a malicious MCP server to be registered already. These are author-reported lab outcomes; the study covers a limited framework set and July 2026 model versions, and does not establish deployment prevalence or independent replication. The linked tool repository README also states that its Distribution License restricts use to authorized security testing, defensive validation and academic research, and prohibits redistribution and modification; the full license and result artifacts were not reviewed.

item.title: China publishes State Council guidance on AI and employment adaptation
item.description: China’s State Council General Office issued an employment-focused AI opinion dated 16 October 2026; Hubei HRSS/Xinhua reports publication on 23 October, and a complete official Ministry of Ecology and Environment copy was posted on 24 October. Its 18 tasks span job creation, employment-friendly AI adoption, training, services, worker and social-security protections, income distribution, and employment-risk monitoring and response. The text calls for assessment of some projects’ employment risks and advance notice and transition support for affected workers. These are policy instructions; implementation and labor-market effects remain unmeasured.

item.title: OpenAI releases a claimed AI-generated refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis with Lean formalization
item.description: OpenAI reports that an internal model produced a refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), then released a natural-language manuscript and Lean formalization. The linked Lean scope describes a subexponential exact-counting bound for fixed-k canonical k-CNF formulas, a formalized statement that would contradict ETH if its definitions and scope match the standard conjecture. OpenAI says an external group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams will examine the result; the group’s participation is not certification. Independent mathematical review, a reproduced build and practical algorithmic consequences remain unestablished.

item.title: Insilico reports preliminary Phase 1 activity for AI-designed pan-TEAD inhibitor ISM6331
item.description: Insilico Medicine reported preliminary Phase 1 results for ISM6331, an investigational pan-TEAD inhibitor designed using its Chemistry42 generative-AI platform. In the company’s 26 October release, it reported a 40.0% ORR at 130 mg among two of five response-evaluable mesothelioma participants, and an 18.2% ORR across 30–130 mg among four of 22 participants. The company reported 36 enrolled participants and ongoing dose escalation at an August 14 data cutoff. These are issuer-reported early-phase results from small denominators; controlled efficacy, independent interpretation and any causal contribution from AI are not established.

item.title: Brazil’s MGI considers stronger rules for federal workers’ use of AI tools
item.description: A Sep 14, 2026 Tele.Síntese interview reported that Brazil’s Management and Innovation Minister Esther Dweck was considering giving an existing ethical-AI-use manual for federal workers stronger force as a Portaria or presidential decree. Dweck also said a federal self-assessment found more than 150 AI solutions already in use and more than 300 initiatives under study or development. The statements document reported policy intent and ministry-reported inventory counts, not an enacted nationwide rule or audited outcomes. A bounded official MGI search found ministry-level governance and guidance but no manual-specific nationwide instrument; a full Diário Oficial check remains open.

item.title: PolyGraph reports plan-buffered CUDA Graph capture for adaptive speculative decoding
item.description: The PolyGraph preprint proposes one maximum-grid CUDA Graph with GPU-resident updates for changing speculative-decoding shapes. Its abstract reports a single-H800 trace-driven prototype that replaces 64 shape-specific graphs with one, gives warmed P50 latency of 17.7 vs 17.8 ms and cuts graph-build time from 3,915 to 93 ms. The author also reports a P99 benefit that depends on padding waste. This is a bounded synthetic-trace result, not a production serving demonstration; independent reproduction remains open. The arXiv page says the v1 was submitted on 14 August 2026 despite the identifier prefix 2610, an unexplained metadata discrepancy.

item.title: ANEEL approves Group A electricity-market migration and Open Energy rules
item.description: ANEEL’s 27 October 2026 announcement says its board approved rule changes for Group A consumers in medium and high voltage and instituted Open Energy. The announcement describes a standardized, consent-based way to access and share consumption, billing and metering data, with an initial comparison page and standardized access due within 12 months of rule publication and API sharing within 24 months. For most simplified AS/A4 cases it reports migration deadlines falling from 180 to 90 days; other cases remain at 180 days. The signed resolutions and Official Gazette publication/effective dates were not retrieved in this check, and no adoption, electricity-price, procurement or data-platform outcome is established.

item.title: Anthropic adds server-side message threads to its Claude API
item.description: Anthropic’s Nov 2, 2026 platform release notes introduced beta message threads for the Claude Messages API and listed availability across Anthropic’s API and three managed cloud platforms. The official documentation says clients create a thread with the full conversation and continue it by sending only new messages plus the prior response ID; the service retains the conversation temporarily. Threads expire after five minutes without a request and are deleted within one hour after last use. Anthropic says this reduces repeated upload, validation and tokenization work, but reports no measured latency or cost results. The feature is not ZDR- or HIPAA-eligible and does not support compaction, context editing, token counting or message batches.

item.title: DepthGraft reports hierarchical cross-layer KV reconstruction with lower cache and prefill cost
item.description: The authors propose hierarchical sharing of key/value (KV) representations across transformer depth, reconstructing deep-layer KV from aligned shallow and middle layers. In experiments on dense and MoE models from 0.5B to 16B parameters, they report a roughly one-third KV-cache reduction. For 9B MLA and 16B GQA models, the paper reports lower time-to-first-token (TTFT) at 8K–128K context and nearly unchanged time-per-output-token (TPOT); at 128K, reported TTFT reductions are 26.8% and 28.8%, respectively. These results are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced.

item.title: KAPPO derives adaptive policy pressure for pass@k and max@k post-training
item.description: The authors derive closed-form optimal policies for KL-regularized pass@k and max@k objectives and identify prompt-adaptive pressure that can be implemented by modifying standard @1 optimization. They report experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation using OLMo-3-7B-Instruct-SFT and Qwen3-4B-Base: KAPPO variants reduce the paper's measured sharpening pattern, and @k-A*PO using one new completion per prompt is reported comparable to PKPO, which requires at least k on-policy completions. These are paper-reported results, not independent reproductions.

item.title: A Qwen looping study reports gains only in its smallest post-training regime
item.description: The authors compare post-training transformer layer loops in Qwen3/Qwen3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B parameters against identically trained unlooped twins and unlooped equal-FLOP controls. In the reported short full-fine-tuning condition, the 0.8B loop improves a paired GSM8K/MATH macro score by 4.1 points, while the main 4B and 9B comparisons show no statistically significant gain. The paper separately evaluates training-free loop conversions: its Qwen3-8B loop has modest or non-significant task gains at about 1.8x measured decoding time, while selected Qwen3-14B results differ. These are author-reported results from specific Qwen recipes and task sets, not evidence about recurrence learned during large-scale pretraining or production workloads.

item.title: Epoch AI revises its Abilene estimate to 1,019k H100e
item.description: Epoch AI’s Nov 1, 2026 update raised its estimated current compute for the OpenAI Stargate Abilene site from 764k to 1,019k H100-equivalents, and its estimated IT power from 618 MW to 824 MW. Epoch says it combines satellite imagery, cooling-equipment power modeling, company disclosures, regulatory filings and drone imagery. Its profile estimates buildings 7–8 operational by analogy to earlier buildout timing, while noting Oracle had not given a date for those final buildings. The revised figures are an independent model estimate, not metered IT load or independently confirmed delivery of the final buildings.

item.title: SafeWebWorld finds plausible web-agent predictions can still omit authorization evidence
item.description: A 29 Oct 2026 arXiv preprint introduces SafeWebWorld, a five-domain benchmark asking whether predicted web actions preserve evidence needed to choose among Execute, Ask, and Block. The authors report that 86.1% of 3,000 matched predictions from ten frozen open models were judged semantically plausible, while plausibility and low false-safe rates could coexist with weak evidence recovery or poor Ask recall. These are author-reported results on constructed cases: one primary reviewer audited the frozen test set, shortcut features remain predictive, and live action outcomes were not tested.

item.title: NVIDIA documents NVKE Kubernetes AI conformance testing on two GB200 workers
item.description: NVIDIA's AICR v1.2.0 release includes an NVKE GB200 training/Kubeflow recipe and publishes a Kubernetes v1.36 AI conformance submission. In the linked submission, NVIDIA says it collected evidence on Oct 27–28, 2026 using NVKE v0.22.0 and Kubernetes v1.36.3 on two ARM64 GB200 workers with eight GPUs. The results matrix marks seven applicable MUST requirements as passed and cluster autoscaling as not applicable under the operator-controlled scaling design. These are vendor-authored results for the described configuration; independent replay or external CNCF acceptance was not established in this review.

item.title: NVIDIA reports Kubernetes validation on two early Vera Rubin NVL72 clusters
item.description: NVIDIA describes bringing an NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) Preview recipe online on two early Vera Rubin NVL72 reference clusters. Its public account says the training recipe passed deployment and conformance checks and a cross-node 16 GiB NCCL all-reduce gate at 744.71 GB/s bus bandwidth. The inference variant passed deployment and conformance only; NVIDIA explicitly says inference-serving performance remains deferred. These are company-reported results for a Preview configuration, not independent reproduction or production qualification.

item.title: PhysRSI-eval reports five-axis measurements of iterative robot-manipulation improvement
item.description: Galbot researchers introduce PhysRSI-eval, a five-axis profile separating first-attempt performance, timing of gains, attained scores, physical interaction budget and recovery from early failure. In the main simulation evaluation, the paper reports six model-plus-runtime systems on 18 manipulation tasks: GPT-6 Astra solved 15, GPT-6.1 Sol 12, GPT-6 Sol 7, GPT-5.6 Sol 1, Claude Opus 5.5 13, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 11. The paper reports that final score, early improvement and budget efficiency can diverge, and exploratory associations between public capability scores and the five outcome axes. It also reports Astra workspace interventions and held-out layout tests. All results remain author-reported. The main comparison has one improvement chain per task; the capability analysis covers six systems without independent validation; Astra's ablation/frozen tests cover six tasks, and transfer evidence comprises three cases.

item.title: OpenAI reports Pando, a Git-compatible backend built for monorepo and agent-scale traffic
item.description: In a 2 November 2026 engineering report, OpenAI describes Pando, a backend that it says now serves all development on its monorepo while retaining compatibility with the Git protocol and client. Its design stores incoming packs as immutable blobs, tracks per-branch ref versions and dependencies, permits unrelated branch writes to proceed independently, and reuses stored packs for fetches. OpenAI reports nearly fivefold lower median push latency and nearly one petabyte of Git data delivered per day in production. These operational figures and deployment details are first-party claims; the article supplies no independently inspected workload traces or external reproduction. The article separately labels its architecture comparison as synthetic teaching simulations rather than production benchmarks.

item.title: Brazil establishes a national digital-health policy covering data governance and emerging technology
item.description: Brazil’s Ministry of Health reported that Portaria GM/MS 12.301 instituted a National Digital Health Information Policy, published in the official gazette on 28 October 2026. The ministry describes a national framework for health-data interoperability, the CPF as a priority user identifier, telehealth, data protection, digital sovereignty and safe, responsible use of emerging technologies. The linked official instrument returned HTTP 502 in this review, so exact operative text—especially any AI-specific duties—was not inspected. The announcement establishes policy direction, not implementation or health outcomes.

item.title: China says AI-assisted labor mediation and arbitration pilots now cover all provincial-level regions
item.description: On 2 November 2026, China’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security reported expanding the “AI+ mediation and arbitration” pilot to all provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps. A May Shenzhen HRSS article says officials from 13 provincial-level jurisdictions shared experience at a workshop; it separately identifies Shenzhen as a designated pilot area in 2025 and does not establish that all 13 attendees were pilot sites or had deployed systems. The article, credited to Nanfang+ client, describes Shenzhen’s local system and reports usage and processing-time metrics that remain unaudited. The national expansion statement does not establish uniform operation, dispute outcomes, fairness, safety or independent effectiveness.

item.title: CausalWAM adds sparse action-relevance routing to a world-action model
item.description: The CausalWAM preprint presents an identifiability result for action-relevant latent factors under support-sparsity assumptions and reports adding a sparse router to a world-action model. In author-run evaluations, the paper reports gains over its baseline on 13 of 17 RoboCasa365 tasks (macro success 0.24 to 0.43), higher results across 40 LIBERO tasks, and a majority of successes over the baseline in 50 Franka cube-stack trials per policy. These are single-preprint results, not independent replications. The implementation retains a dense visual-to-action path; the paper's routed-only intervention covers four selected high-success tasks and does not establish that the learned theoretical support alone drives actions generally.

item.title: Jiangsu sets AI employment monitoring and skills-training targets
item.description: Jiangsu's provincial government office published a September 29, 2026 employment-policy notice that calls for assessing the employment effects of major policies and public investment and establishing a survey of AI's effects on jobs and skills. For labor-intensive sectors, it says the province will explore minimum human-participation standards and a displacement buffer period. The notice also sets a target of one million person-times of AI-field technical-skills training during the fifteenth Five-Year Plan period. These are announced measures and targets; the notice does not show funding, delivery, implementation or employment effects. The policy predates and is separate from China's later October 16 national AI-employment opinion.

item.title: ACCT reports cross-model context-state transfer across three model families
item.description: A preprint introduces ACCT, which converts KV states already computed by one model into sparse KV states that a different-size model in the same family can use without re-encoding the full context. Across six directed pairs in Qwen3, Llama and Qwen2.5, authors report 4x KV-slot compression and mixed task results. The 6.5–21.2x speed headline measures conversion against target prefill and excludes source-model prefill. Appendix K includes source prefill: at the longest tested context, only three smaller-to-larger directions are faster than target-only prefill, while reverse directions are slower. These are author-reported experiments, not independent production evidence.

item.title: A conditional optimization method allocates inference budgets across complementary language models
item.description: An October 29 arXiv paper studies allocating repeated-sampling inference budgets across language models. It proves the general allocation problem NP-hard and gives an efficient global optimization method under a stated diminishing-returns condition: each model’s per-query log-failure reduction must be nondecreasing and concave in spend. On four coding and agentic benchmarks, the authors report a better solve-rate/cost frontier than any single model, with larger gains where model strengths complement one another; a greedy sequential order is within 10% of the best fixed order at median, while cheapest-first can spend up to 16% more. The results use recorded trials, sometimes only four or five per model/query, and a mix of observed prices, public price snapshots and compute proxies. They are paper-reported, not an independent reproduction or evidence of real marketplace revenue and price effects.

item.title: LLM-built simple baselines recover much of published deep-learning gains across 36 scientific prediction tasks
item.description: An October 28 arXiv preprint reports that one Claude Opus 5 workflow constructed supervised prediction baselines across 36 tasks reconstructed from selected open-access papers in Nature-, Science- and Cell-family journals. Across task medians, the authors report a median simple-baseline strength of 95.5% and a mean of 85.7%; on 12 tasks the median baseline matched or exceeded the published deep-learning score. The result is a bounded author-reported audit of predictive contributions, not evidence that the source studies are invalid or that predictive accuracy captures interpretability or scientific insight.

item.title: A premise-first audit finds limited selection signal, modest realized speedup, and compute-dependent render corruption in one world-action-model stack
item.description: A preprint by Liu et al. audits test-time scaling on Cosmos Policy in RoboCasa. In that configuration, the authors report that their deployable value selector performed 1.66 percentage points below random selection; a hindsight oracle gained 1.40 points, with an episode-level interval spanning zero, while 82% of tested states had identical candidate outcomes. Token pruning removed up to 47.9% of per-forward FLOPs but delivered at most 1.152× measured end-to-end speedup on the deployed path (1.253× with future-image decoding excluded), below a pre-registered 1.5× target. A power gate halted the full adaptive-allocation experiment, so its effect remains unresolved. The authors also identify a silent OpenGL render corruption in the tested RoboCasa/robosuite stack, report a detector and fix, and find the corruption more frequent in a non-standard compute-heavy planning path; they say the official direct-policy benchmark is not materially affected. These are author-reported, configuration-specific findings, not evidence that test-time scaling generally fails.

item.title: European Commission proposes a Cloud and AI Development Act with capacity and sovereignty measures
item.description: On 3 June 2026, the European Commission proposed the Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA), combining measures to accelerate sustainable data-centre deployment with a common cloud and AI sovereignty framework and coordinated public-sector procurement. The proposal aims to at least triple EU data-centre capacity within five to seven years. Its impact assessment estimates that EU27 installed capacity would reach 12.4 GW in 2025 while supply fell almost 3 GW short of estimated demand; its market figures rely on an external study that excludes private enterprise sites, including many dedicated HPC facilities. As of the 2026-11-02 check, Parliament listed the proposal as awaiting committee decision. These remain proposal terms and Commission estimates, not enacted policy or verified market-wide outcomes.

item.title: Latent Sparse Attention reports long-context attention speedups up to 10M tokens
item.description: A preprint introduces Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), which clusters keys in a learned latent space so queries search cluster summaries rather than score every key. In author-run tests, its distilled form stayed near the tested model baselines at contexts up to 10M tokens and reduced attention-layer prefill and decode time substantially on two specific model families and H200/B300 hardware. The paper reports smaller end-to-end serving gains than the per-layer headline; its 100M-token result is an extrapolation. The linked implementation could not be accessed during this review, and no independent reproduction was performed.

item.title: Google and Oracle announce planned TPU capacity on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
item.description: Google Cloud and Oracle announced plans to deploy Google TPU capacity on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure starting in 2027. The Google Cloud Blog and Oracle press release describe OCI as the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer TPUs; Oracle says availability will ramp over multiple years, and its Chinese-language post describes a plan to reach gigawatt scale. This is a distinct announced supply route from Oracle’s NVIDIA accelerator expansion. The announcements establish the partnership and plans, not delivered capacity, customer adoption, OCI-specific TPU performance or economics.

item.title: Canada announces a staged equity investment of up to C$1.6 billion in Cohere
item.description: On Oct 29, 2026, Canada announced a planned commercial equity investment of up to C$1.6 billion in Cohere, to be made in stages alongside private investors. The government release says Cohere committed to at least 1,000 new Canadian technical jobs and C$1.7 billion in additional Canadian compute infrastructure by 2030. These are announced future terms; the release does not establish disbursement, completed hiring or delivered compute. A prior C$725 million Cohere/CoreWeave compute project is separately documented, and public records reviewed do not reconcile any overlap between the new job and compute commitments and Cohere’s Oct 30 aggregate plan.

item.title: Cohere reports a C$4 billion Canada investment and 1,500-plus job plan through 2031
item.description: In an Oct 30, 2026 company post, Cohere described an update to its Canada investment effort, which it said began in 2024. The company expects the multi-year effort to create more than 1,500 jobs and deliver more than C$4 billion in research-and-development and AI-infrastructure investment through 2031, including at least 1,000 technical roles. These are company projections, not independently verified spending or hiring outcomes. Cohere does not quantify how much is new against the existing effort. The government announced a separate staged equity investment on Oct 29; the public sources reviewed do not reconcile overlap between the plans or with the prior C$725 million compute project.

item.title: A paper argues that latent monitors must separate prompt-injection exposure from unsafe-action commitment
item.description: A paper reports that latent monitors trained on a mixed unsafe-versus-rest contrast can flag prompt-injection exposure without reliably predicting which exposed agent will take an unsafe tool action. In a generated-action AgentDojo grid, Qwen's naive contrast gives pre-action AUROC 0.556 for NLA text and 0.672 for an activation probe; training on exposed cases only raises the activation probe to 0.853, close to a matched visible-text TF-IDF baseline at 0.855. The paper reports related commitment-contrast results on Mistral-7B and OLMo-2-7B, but all three model families use AgentDojo and the generated-action study is not a live rollout.

item.title: China issues a recommended technical standard for large-model inference platforms
item.description: China's national standards catalogue records YD/T 7171—2026 as a recommended communications industry standard for large-model inference platforms, published on 2026-07-15 and effective from 2026-11-01. Its stated scope covers model compression, deployment, inference, platform services and management and provides functional reference for institutions using such platforms. The catalogue does not establish mandatory adoption, organization-level compliance or measured implementation outcomes.

item.title: A 41-country paper reports a shift toward senior workers at AI-adopting multinationals
item.description: A September 2026 Stanford Digital Economy Lab working paper analyzes 1.25 billion job postings and 154 million employment records across 41 countries, inferring firm AI adoption from generative-AI job advertisements. In an instrumented event study of foreign multinational affiliates, the authors report a 1.9-percentage-point decline in junior workforce share by March 2026 relative to matched controls. Senior employment rises 6.7%; the 2.5% decline estimate for junior employment is not statistically significant, and total employment rises 3.3% at marginal significance. The authors interpret their model-based decomposition as suggestive of modest, seniority-biased productivity gains. These are paper-reported estimates, not independent replication or a representative global labor census. The paper notes platform coverage and adoption-timing limits and an untestable instrument exclusion restriction. A King's College London summary gives a conflicting record count and reverses the paper period; Stanford's official page and the paper support the 154 million / 2021–March 2026 figures recorded here. Its population and adoption measure differ from Anthropic’s October 2026 internal workforce report, so it is comparative evidence rather than a replication.

item.title: UK and Google DeepMind report early PlanAssist results as live pilot expands to 15 councils
item.description: The UK government says early PlanAssist testing in Barnet, Camden and Dorset cut officer time on key householder-application tasks by 58% and links that result to a reduction in routine processing from eight weeks to four. Google DeepMind reports that more than 70% of generated reports needed no edits. Both are involved-party claims without disclosed pilot denominators or comparison design. The official tender defines the eight-to-four-week target around stages the tool can affect and excludes consultation, site visits, neighbour notification, external-consultee responses and committee scheduling, so the broader end-to-end implication is not established. PlanningLens reports a 7.71-week pre-trial median across 7,663 decisions and a matched 16-council panel frozen before outcomes; its early May–July data are not attributed to the tool, and it says results are too early. The official award notice lists £8.288 million including VAT for a contract to Google Cloud EMEA Limited, not realized spend or proven value. The live test expands to 15 councils for 12 months, with officers retaining review and decision authority.

item.title: OpenConjecture study highlights why mathematical outputs need intent and novelty review
item.description: Helen Jenne, Davis Brown, Jesse He and Henry Kvinge introduce OpenConjecture, a dataset of conjectures drawn from recent mathematics preprints, and analyze a random sample of 200 conjectures from 200 papers. Across three successive GPT-model passes, the authors report proposed proofs or counterexamples for 125 items; 84% passed a review by a new instance of the same model that generated each response. The paper explicitly does not treat those outcomes as expert-verified solutions. Its analyses flag cases where counterexamples appear to exploit missing assumptions or depart from authors’ intended meaning, and where proofs follow existing results. The work argues that mathematical-agent evaluation should assess fidelity to the stated problem, relationship to prior literature, attribution and novelty, in addition to formal or literal correctness. It is a first-party, non-expert-verified study, not a measured rate of newly solved open problems.

item.title: OpenFrontiers separates mathematical rediscovery from retrieval of known solutions
item.description: Jiarui Yao, Ruida Wang and Tong Zhang introduce OpenFrontiers, a research-problem corpus of 12,151 records and a retrospective mathematics benchmark of 200 problems. The benchmark separates 110 problems with located 2026 solutions from 90 listed as open at the authors’ status check, and supplies a Lean 4 statement for each item. In an author-reported evaluation of seven LLM agents on a selected 50-item subset, closed-book agents solved at most 7 of 40 resolved items; most live-web successes followed retrieval of an existing solution. This is a paper-reported benchmark result, not independent evidence about general scientific ability. The corpus is 93.4% mathematics, nearly half its records are marked unassessed, and 1,562 of its 1,946 Lean attachments contain a lexical placeholder flag. The authors state that uncertain upstream status is retained rather than treated as proof a problem remains open.

item.title: China’s NDRC and five ministries announce 136 major application-scenario projects
item.description: China’s National Development and Reform Commission and five other central departments announced a first portfolio of 136 major application-scenario projects on 20 October 2026. The NDRC says the portfolio spans five categories and involves more than 1,700 technologies, 1,200 products and 2,200 standards or specifications; it also describes plans to open eligible validation opportunities to private and smaller firms and to support follow-through. A Beijing government article names five municipal projects in the list, including a 6G validation environment and an industrial-network/data-security agent service. These sources establish the announcement and selected examples, not the complete project list, AI-specific share, project funding, operational status, user access or measured technical and economic outcomes.

item.title: Canada joins EuroHPC as its 39th participating state
item.description: On 30 October 2026, Canada became the 39th participating state in the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, which pools public resources for supercomputing and related research. EuroHPC and the European Commission say Canadian scientists will be able to access European HPC, AI and quantum resources. EuroHPC’s current Regular Access call states that organizations in Horizon Europe-associated countries may apply for post-2020 EuroHPC supercomputers; the Commission says Canada has been associated with Horizon Europe since 2024. Applications remain subject to the call’s employment, review and formal-allocation requirements. No Canadian award, usage or resulting research or economic outcome was inspected.

item.title: OpenAI describes expanded frontier-model misalignment monitoring and a live training alert
item.description: OpenAI’s Oct 29 disclosure describes a layered system for monitoring frontier-model training, evaluations, internal agent use and selected external tool use. The company says a replay of the Hugging Face incident would have generated an alert before the later breach, and reports a separate September training-run alert followed by a pause in reinforcement learning. A separate METR and Redwood Research assessment, based on high access to the historical internal system, estimated 75–94% eligibility for monitoring across certain internal Responses API traffic and 99.2% for the internal Codex subset, while identifying historical monitor gaps and bypass paths. Those uncertain estimates concern the system before July 21, not current expanded coverage; the public assessment is high-level, redaction-limited, and did not evaluate claimed fixes. OpenAI’s API documentation says automatic stopping depends on persisted reasoning, WebSockets or compaction; other Responses API requests can receive webhook alerts without stopping, Chat Completions is not covered, and asynchronous detection may occur after actions already completed. OpenAI also reports selected layer-2 recall figures: 79.6% for immediate escalation on its real-incident set and 59.6% on its synthetic set, with higher rates for less urgent review; immediate escalation on one step-by-step sabotage set was 43.6%. The article gives no sample denominators or false-positive rates for these tables.

item.title: Beijing AI+ Conference reports launch of ReAct-Manip robot adaptation evaluation set
item.description: An official Beijing AI+ Conference recap dated October 31 says the event launched ReAct-Manip, a robot operation-adaptation evaluation set. The recap names the benchmark but gives no technical specification, scores or model comparisons. A separate news report also describes the release. The PyPI ReAct-Manip v0.3 package has not been tied to the conference announcement, so its protocol and any capability implications remain unestablished.

item.title: Renmin University publishes report of a proposed China-linked international AI cooperation framework
item.description: On November 1, Renmin University’s official news site published a China Daily-sourced report about a whitepaper release at the October 31 Beijing AI+ Conference. The report says Renmin University’s Gaoling School of AI and the China-SCO AI Application Cooperation Center were core compilers, with 24 other institutions listed as co-authors. It summarizes a proposed framework combining capability building, application cooperation and governance coordination, with models, compute and corpora described as shared technical infrastructure. These are claims reported by the article; the full whitepaper and independent partner-country evaluation were not recovered.

item.title: Japan begins phased government AI-agent rollout under a new governance standard
item.description: Japan’s Digital Agency announced a prototype parliamentary-answer drafting app on its Government AI platform for a trial during the 222nd extraordinary Diet session, with about 180,000 government employees eligible. The agency says 102 officials from 16 ministries evaluated development and about 80% of survey respondents wanted to use the prototype; the respondent denominator and method are not reported, and stated interest is not evidence of adoption or effectiveness. Officials retain source checking, policy judgment and responsibility for final answers. No measured accuracy, time, cost or safety outcome is reported.

item.title: LongChang tests free exploration for evidence-supported discovery in simulated physics
item.description: The LongChang preprint reports a benchmark for whether language models can notice unexpected behavior in simulated physical worlds, choose questions and test altered physical laws without assigned research tasks or hints. Across 12 models and 15 fixed-start MuJoCo scenes, the authors report a 16.7% discovery rate for GPT-6-Astra and 0% for the other 11 models; discovery required both correct law identification and evidence support. In the ordinary-physics control, 36.1% of reports were rejected for false anomalies or unsupported explanations.
